facts.content: Patient presents with breathing difficulty after a wasp sting about 15 minutes ago.
facts.source_text: CC: Breathing difficulty after wasp sting ~15 min ago

facts.content: Patient was stung by a wasp while gardening.
After the sting, the patient developed shallow breathing.
After the sting, the patient experienced chest tightness.
After the sting, the patient noticed lip tingling.
After the sting, the patient developed a blotchy rash.
The patient reports no throat tightness or closure.
The patient reports no prior similar reactions to stings.
The patient has taken no medications yet for this reaction.
The patient has an over-the-counter antihistamine available at home.
Patient has a history of eczema.
Patient has a history of aerosinusitis.
facts.source_text: PMH: Eczema; aerosinusitis (uses antihistamines for flying)

facts.content: Patient uses antihistamines when flying due to aerosinusitis.
Patient is not taking any regular medications.
Patient is allergic to penicillin.
The patient's wife is present at home and assisting.
facts.source_text: SH: Wife present at home and assisting

facts.content: Clinician assesses an allergic reaction to a wasp sting with concern for evolving anaphylaxis due to respiratory symptoms and mucocutaneous findings.
facts.source_text: Allergic reaction to wasp stingconcern for evolving anaphylaxis (respiratory sx + mucocutaneous findings)

facts.content: Plan is to call an ambulance immediately and avoid self-transport.
The patient's wife initiated the ambulance call during the consult.
Patient is advised to take an oral antihistamine now while awaiting the ambulance.
facts.source_text: Take oral antihistamine now while awaiting ambulance

facts.content: Plan is for emergency department evaluation and management due to risk of rapid progression and anaphylaxis.
facts.source_text: ED evaluation/management due to risk of rapid progression/anaphylaxis

facts.content: The rationale for emergency department evaluation was discussed and the patient agrees.
